.github/workflows/ci.yml.text:
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings

jobs:
  # Workaround for making GitHub Actions skip based on commit message `[skip ci]`.
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: |
      !contains(format('{0} {1} {2}', github.event.head_commit.message, github.event.pull_request.title, github.event.pull_request.body), '[skip ci]')
    steps:
      - run: |
          cat <<'MESSAGE'
          github.event_name: ${{ toJson(github.event_name) }}
          github.event:
          ${{ toJson(github.event) }}
          MESSAGE

  fmt:
    name: rustfmt
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt
      - run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  clippy:
    name: clippy (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.features }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Run clippy on macOS and Windows too so the `cfg(target_os …)`
        # branches (macOS peercred via getpeereid; Windows Job Object /
        # LockFileEx / DACL) get lint-checked pre-merge instead of waiting
        # for the release matrix to surface a regression.
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        # Run with and without `uat` so neither side rots:
        # - `test-fixtures` alone is the shape the release binary ships.
        # - `test-fixtures,uat` compiles `src/cli/uat/*` (gated behind
        #   `#[cfg(feature = "uat")]`) and lint-checks the maintainer-only
        #   surface. Cheap insurance — UAT module sits behind one cfg
        #   gate, and a future change that accidentally couples non-UAT
        #   code to a UAT-only item gets caught here, not when a release
        #   binary refuses to build.
        features: ["test-fixtures", "test-fixtures,uat"]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --features ${{ matrix.features }} -- -D warnings

  test:
    name: test (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.features }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        # See `clippy` for the feature-matrix rationale. The `uat`
        # feature adds ~52 hermetic tests (unit + `tests/uat_lifecycle_test.rs`
        # backend-mismatch path); none of them require a GPU because
        # pre-flight fails before any subprocess spawns. The full
        # GPU-touching lifecycle lives on the nightly Metal lane plus
        # maintainer-run per-release UAT — never on PR CI.
        features: ["test-fixtures", "test-fixtures,uat"]
        # macOS sets `$TMPDIR` to /var/folders/<a>/<b>/T/ (~49 chars);
        # historical socket-path tests needed /tmp to stay under macOS's
        # sun_path limit. The HTTP-loopback transport removed that
        # constraint (Unit 4 of the Windows+HTTP-IPC plan) but pinning
        # /tmp is still cheap and avoids any other long-path surprise.
        # Windows uses the runner's default temp dir (no TMPDIR override).
        # Test concurrency is bounded by nextest's `daemon-bound`
        # test-group (.config/nextest.toml): it caps how many
        # daemon-spawning tests run at once across the whole run —
        # globally, not per-binary like libtest's old `--test-threads`
        # band-aid. Each such test boots a full daemon (control plane +
        # proxy listener + supervised tasks); several at once
        # oversubscribe a 3-4 core runner and starve a listener past its
        # readiness deadline (the off-Linux flake). The `ci` profile also
        # retries to absorb any residual environmental flake.
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            tmpdir_override: /tmp
          - os: macos-latest
            tmpdir_override: /tmp
          - os: windows-latest
            tmpdir_override: ""
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.87.5
        with:
          tool: nextest
      - name: cargo nextest run
        run: cargo nextest run --profile ci --features ${{ matrix.features }} --workspace
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
          TMPDIR: ${{ matrix.tmpdir_override }}
      # nextest doesn't run doctests — cover them separately.
      - name: cargo test --doc
        run: cargo test --doc --features ${{ matrix.features }} --workspace
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
          TMPDIR: ${{ matrix.tmpdir_override }}

  test-no-features:
    # Validates that unit tests (--lib) pass without any feature flags.
    # Catches accidental dependencies on test-only surface — AGENTS.md
    # requires CI to run both with and without `test-fixtures`.
    name: test (no features)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo test --lib
        run: cargo test --lib --no-fail-fast
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

  msrv:
    # Ensures the declared MSRV (Cargo.toml rust-version) stays honest.
    # Uses `cargo check --locked` so a dep bump past the declared MSRV
    # is caught here.
    name: msrv (1.95)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # The action's ref tag doubles as the toolchain version, so a
      # Dependabot bump ("@1.95" -> "@1.100") installs a nonexistent
      # release and 404s. Pin the toolchain explicitly; the ref floats.
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.95"
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo check --locked
        run: cargo check --locked

  audit:
    # Dependency vulnerability scan via `cargo audit`. Fails on any
    # advisory with a non-zero severity (--deny warnings).
    name: cargo audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - name: install cargo-audit
        run: cargo install cargo-audit --locked
      - name: cargo audit
        run: cargo audit --deny warnings

  doc:
    # Ensures doc comments compile without warnings. Uses RUSTDOCFLAGS
    # so broken intra-doc links and invalid HTML tags fail the build.
    # --all-features so the feature-gated modules are documented too: the
    # `uat` subcommand carried two invalid HTML tags that the default-feature
    # build never looked at.
    name: cargo doc
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features
        run: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings

  cross-aarch64:
    name: cross-compile aarch64-linux
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: install cross-linker
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
      - name: cargo check
        run: cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --release
        env:
          CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc

  nightly-coverage:
    # Keep one Ubuntu-only nightly lane for unstable-regression detection and
    # coverage publication; stable + macOS lanes above already cover the main
    # matrix, so we avoid doubling the expensive jobs.
    name: nightly coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          components: rustc, rust-std, cargo, llvm-tools, llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: clean stale stable artifacts
        run: cargo clean
      - name: create coverage directory
        run: mkdir -p ./target/debug/coverage
      - name: install grcov
        run: cargo install grcov --locked
      - name: cargo test nightly
        run: cargo test --features test-fixtures,uat --workspace --no-fail-fast
        env:
          CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
          LLVM_PROFILE_FILE: "target/debug/coverage/llamastash-%p-%m.profraw"
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
          RUSTFLAGS: "-Cinstrument-coverage -Cpanic=abort -Zpanic_abort_tests"
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: "-C instrument-coverage -Cpanic=abort -Zpanic_abort_tests -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests target/debug/"
          TMPDIR: /tmp
      - name: bundle raw coverage profiles
        run: zip ./target/debug/coverage/files.zip ./target/debug/coverage/llamastash-*.profraw
      - name: grcov
        run: |
          grcov ./target/debug/coverage/files.zip \
            -s . \
            --binary-path ./target/debug/ \
            -o ./target/debug/coverage/lcov.info \
            --branch \
            --ignore-not-existing \
            --llvm \
            --filter covered \
            --ignore '/*' \
            --ignore 'C:/*' \
            --ignore '../*' \
            -t lcov
      - name: Push grcov results to Coveralls
        uses: coverallsapp/github-action@v2
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          file: ./target/debug/coverage/lcov.info
          format: lcov

  actionlint:
    # Static analysis for the workflow YAML themselves. Catches expression
    # mistakes, shell quoting bugs, deprecated keywords, and similar shape
    # issues that would otherwise only surface when a release.yml regression
    # detonates mid-tag.
    name: actionlint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: install actionlint + shellcheck
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck
          # Pin to a specific actionlint release for reproducibility.
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhysd/actionlint/main/scripts/download-actionlint.bash \
            | bash -s -- 1.7.7
          ./actionlint -version
      - name: actionlint
        run: ./actionlint -color

  release-readiness:
    # Pre-tag guards that catch release-breaking PRs *before* a maintainer
    # cuts a tag. Each check is cheap and fast; running them on every PR
    # means the release workflow never fails for reasons a PR could have
    # surfaced.
    name: release readiness
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    needs: prepare
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: cargo publish --dry-run
        # Validates Cargo.toml manifest shape, license, README presence, and
        # the published file set. Does NOT verify crate-name availability.
        run: cargo publish --dry-run --locked

      - name: changelog has unreleased heading
        # On PRs we just want SOMETHING under [Unreleased]; the tag-time
        # Cargo.toml ↔ CHANGELOG ↔ tag cross-check lives in release.yml's
        # `prepare-release` job, so duplicating it here only fires noise
        # on the release-prep PR (where the maintainer is already paying
        # attention) and on every commit between the Cargo.toml bump and
        # the tag. Keep this lightweight presence guard only.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! grep -q '^## \[Unreleased\]' CHANGELOG.md; then
            echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md is missing the [Unreleased] section header."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "[Unreleased] heading present; OK"

      - name: packager.py unit tests
        # Catches template / argv regressions in the homebrew packager before
        # the release workflow tries to use it.
        run: python3 deployment/homebrew/packager_test.py

      - name: AUR packager.py unit tests
        # Same intent for the AUR packager (publish-aur-source / publish-aur-bin).
        run: python3 deployment/aur/packager_test.py

      - name: Scoop packager.py unit tests
        # Same intent for the Scoop bucket packager (publish-scoop).
        run: python3 deployment/scoop/packager_test.py

      - name: uat — R4 audit (release build never ships --features uat)
        # The shipped binary on crates.io / Homebrew must not carry the
        # maintainer-only `uat` Cargo feature. The release workflow may
        # legitimately use `--features uat` in pre-build validation jobs;
        # what must never happen is adding it to a `cargo build ... --bin
        # llamastash --locked` line that produces the shipped tarballs.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if grep -nE '^[^#]*cargo build .*--features[[:space:]]+uat.*--bin[[:space:]]+llamastash' .github/workflows/release.yml; then
            echo "::error::release.yml adds '--features uat' to a shipped cargo build line — that would ship the maintainer-only UAT subcommand to end users."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "R4: shipped cargo build lines in release.yml do not pass --features uat; OK"

      - name: uat — synthetic exit codes documented
        # Agents parsing `failure_summary.exit_code` rely on the synthetic
        # code table in docs/testing/hardware-uat.md. Each crate-private
        # constant in src/cli/uat/lifecycle.rs must appear in the doc so
        # downstream tooling never sees an undocumented magic number.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          doc=docs/testing/hardware-uat.md
          for sym in PREFLIGHT_MISMATCH_CODE SMOKE_HTTP_ERROR_CODE \
                     SMOKE_PARSE_ERROR_CODE SMOKE_STATUS_ERROR_CODE \
                     TIMEOUT_CODE SIGINT_CODE; do
            if ! grep -qF "$sym" "$doc"; then
              echo "::error::synthetic exit-code constant $sym is missing from $doc"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "all synthetic UAT exit-code constants are documented in $doc; OK"

      - name: uat — nightly workflow carries ce-review fix lock-ins
        # Three ce-review fixes that have textual signatures in the
        # nightly workflow. Reverting any of them silently would
        # re-introduce a flagged regression class — guard accordingly.
        #
        # M-P2-12: gh issue body via --body-file (shell-escape safe).
        # M-P3-05: gh issue list with --limit 1 + title filter.
        # M-P3-07: brew formula version folded into the cache key.
        # M-P2-07: HF cache path is the stable runner root, not the
        #          ephemeral sandbox HF_HOME under /tmp.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          nightly=.github/workflows/uat-metal-nightly.yml
          if [ ! -f "$nightly" ]; then
            echo "::notice::$nightly absent — skipping UAT nightly shape audit (spike-fail collapse path)"
            exit 0
          fi
          fail=0
          if ! grep -qF -- "--body-file" "$nightly"; then
            echo "::error::$nightly: gh issue comment must use --body-file (ce-review M-P2-12)"
            fail=1
          fi
          if ! grep -qF -- "--limit 1" "$nightly"; then
            echo "::error::$nightly: gh issue list must use --limit 1 (ce-review M-P3-05)"
            fail=1
          fi
          if ! grep -qF "brew info" "$nightly"; then
            echo "::error::$nightly: brew formula version must be folded into the cache key (ce-review M-P3-07)"
            fail=1
          fi
          # The HF cache path on `actions/cache@v4` must NOT be the
          # default `~/.cache/huggingface/hub` — the UAT sandbox redirects
          # HF_HOME, so caching the default path is a permanent miss
          # (M-P2-07).
          if grep -qE 'path:.*~/\.cache/huggingface/hub' "$nightly"; then
            echo "::error::$nightly: cache must target the stable HF root (steps.hf-cache.outputs.dir), not ~/.c

.github/workflows/publish-aur-manual.yml.text:
name: publish-aur-manual

# Manual recovery + initial-test workflow for the publish-aur-* steps in
# release.yml. Use when:
#
#   - The release.yml AUR job(s) failed but cargo publish / homebrew already
#     succeeded — re-running release.yml would re-publish to crates.io, which
#     fails on the duplicate version. This workflow re-does ONLY the AUR push.
#   - Bootstrapping AUR publishing for the first time. Trigger this workflow
#     against an existing GH Release tag (e.g. v0.0.1) BEFORE adding the
#     AUR_SSH_KEY secret to the auto path -- if the manual run works end to
#     end, the integrated release.yml jobs will too.
#
# Inputs:
#   release-tag   — existing GH Release tag whose source + .tar.gz.sha256
#                   sidecars feed the PKGBUILDs (e.g. v0.0.1). Must already
#                   exist and must NOT be a prerelease (AUR pkgver disallows
#                   `-`; the packager.py would reject it anyway).
#   variant       — which AUR variant to publish. `all` fires all three jobs;
#                   the variant-specific values fire just one.
#   template-ref  — source ref used for the templates + packager.py.
#                   Defaults to "main" so a hotfix on main can drive a re-run
#                   WITHOUT having to move the release tag.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release-tag:
        description: "Existing GH Release tag to publish (e.g. v0.0.1)"
        required: true
        type: string
      variant:
        description: "Which AUR variant to publish"
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - all
          - llamastash
          - llamastash-bin
          - llamastash-git
        default: all
      template-ref:
        description: "Source ref for templates + packager.py (default: main)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: main

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # Per-tag + per-variant so two simultaneous runs against different variants
  # don't fight over the same AUR repo. `all` shares the lock with itself
  # because the three jobs inside don't touch each other's AUR remote.
  group: publish-aur-manual-${{ inputs.release-tag }}-${{ inputs.variant }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  validate:
    name: validate inputs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - name: validate tag shape + release exists + not a prerelease
        id: tag
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Stable tags only: AUR pkgver disallows `-`, and the packager.py
          # VERSION_RE is X.Y.Z only.
          if ! printf '%s' "$RELEASE_TAG" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
            echo "::error::invalid release-tag: $RELEASE_TAG (expected vX.Y.Z stable; prerelease tags are not publishable to AUR)"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::no GH Release exists for tag $RELEASE_TAG in ${{ github.repository }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          version="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
          printf 'version=%s\n' "$version" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  publish-aur-source:
    name: publish AUR (source)
    needs: [validate]
    if: inputs.variant == 'all' || inputs.variant == 'llamastash'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ needs.validate.outputs.version }}
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.template-ref }}

      - name: compute source-tarball SHA-256
        id: shasum
        env:
          TAG: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha=$(curl -fsSL "https://github.com/llamastash/llamastash/archive/refs/tags/${TAG}.tar.gz" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')
          if ! printf '%s' "$sha" | grep -Eq '^[a-f0-9]{64}$'; then
            echo "::error::source tarball sha-256 did not match expected shape: $sha"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf 'sha=%s\n' "$sha" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: packager_test.py
        run: python3 deployment/aur/packager_test.py

      - name: render PKGBUILD
        env:
          SHA_SOURCE: ${{ steps.shasum.outputs.sha }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p stage
          python3 deployment/aur/packager.py llamastash \
            "$RELEASE_VERSION" \
            deployment/aur/llamastash/PKGBUILD.template \
            stage/PKGBUILD \
            "$SHA_SOURCE"

      - name: generate .SRCINFO + namcap (in archlinux container)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD/stage:/w" -w /w archlinux:base-devel bash -c '
            set -euo pipefail
            pacman -Sy --noconfirm --needed --quiet namcap >/dev/null
            useradd -m b
            chown -R b /w
            su -c "cd /w && makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO && namcap PKGBUILD || true" b
          '

      - name: install AUR SSH key + known_hosts
        env:
          AUR_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.AUR_SSH_KEY }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${AUR_SSH_KEY:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::AUR_SSH_KEY secret is unset; cannot push to AUR"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$AUR_SSH_KEY" >~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          ssh-keyscan -t ed25519,rsa,ecdsa aur.archlinux.org >~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: clone + push aur-llamastash (retry on non-fast-forward)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config --global user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git config --global user.name  "llamastash-release-bot"
          git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/llamastash.git aur-pkg
          cp stage/PKGBUILD stage/.SRCINFO aur-pkg/
          cd aur-pkg
          git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
          if git diff-index --quiet HEAD; then
            echo "aur-llamastash already up to date for ${RELEASE_TAG}; nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(pkg): bump llamastash to ${RELEASE_TAG}"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git push origin master; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "push attempt ${attempt} failed; pulling --rebase and retrying"
            git pull --rebase origin master
            sleep $((attempt * 5))
          done
          echo "::error::AUR push (llamastash) failed after 3 attempts; inspect manually"
          exit 1

  publish-aur-bin:
    name: publish AUR (bin)
    needs: [validate]
    if: inputs.variant == 'all' || inputs.variant == 'llamastash-bin'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RELEASE_VERSION: ${{ needs.validate.outputs.version }}
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.template-ref }}

      - name: download per-target .sha256 sidecars from the GH Release
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Build-job sha-* artifacts expire after 7 days. Recover the
          # canonical sha sidecars from the GH Release itself, which are
          # immutable for as long as the release exists.
          mkdir -p sha-stash
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            if gh release download "$RELEASE_TAG" \
                 --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
                 --pattern '*-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz.sha256' \
                 --dir sha-stash \
                 --clobber; then
              break
            fi
            echo "download attempt ${attempt} failed; sleeping ${attempt}s"
            sleep "$attempt"
          done
          ls -la sha-stash

      - name: extract per-target sha256s
        id: shas
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          extract() {
            local triple="$1"
            local f="sha-stash/llamastash-${RELEASE_VERSION}-${triple}.tar.gz.sha256"
            if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
              echo "::error::missing sha256 sidecar for ${triple}: $f" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            awk '{print $1; exit}' "$f"
          }
          {
            echo "sha_x86_64_linux_gnu=$(extract x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)"
            echo "sha_aarch64_linux_gnu=$(extract aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu)"
          } >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97  # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: packager_test.py
        run: python3 deployment/aur/packager_test.py

      - name: render PKGBUILD
        env:
          SHA_X86_64: ${{ steps.shas.outputs.sha_x86_64_linux_gnu }}
          SHA_AARCH64: ${{ steps.shas.outputs.sha_aarch64_linux_gnu }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p stage
          python3 deployment/aur/packager.py llamastash-bin \
            "$RELEASE_VERSION" \
            deployment/aur/llamastash-bin/PKGBUILD.template \
            stage/PKGBUILD \
            "$SHA_X86_64" \
            "$SHA_AARCH64"

      - name: generate .SRCINFO + namcap (in archlinux container)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD/stage:/w" -w /w archlinux:base-devel bash -c '
            set -euo pipefail
            pacman -Sy --noconfirm --needed --quiet namcap >/dev/null
            useradd -m b
            chown -R b /w
            su -c "cd /w && makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO && namcap PKGBUILD || true" b
          '

      - name: install AUR SSH key + known_hosts
        env:
          AUR_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.AUR_SSH_KEY }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${AUR_SSH_KEY:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::AUR_SSH_KEY secret is unset; cannot push to AUR"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$AUR_SSH_KEY" >~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          ssh-keyscan -t ed25519,rsa,ecdsa aur.archlinux.org >~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: clone + push aur-llamastash-bin (retry on non-fast-forward)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config --global user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git config --global user.name  "llamastash-release-bot"
          git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/llamastash-bin.git aur-pkg
          cp stage/PKGBUILD stage/.SRCINFO aur-pkg/
          cd aur-pkg
          git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
          if git diff-index --quiet HEAD; then
            echo "aur-llamastash-bin already up to date for ${RELEASE_TAG}; nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(pkg): bump llamastash-bin to ${RELEASE_TAG}"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git push origin master; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "push attempt ${attempt} failed; pulling --rebase and retrying"
            git pull --rebase origin master
            sleep $((attempt * 5))
          done
          echo "::error::AUR push (llamastash-bin) failed after 3 attempts; inspect manually"
          exit 1

  publish-aur-git:
    name: publish AUR (git)
    needs: [validate]
    if: inputs.variant == 'all' || inputs.variant == 'llamastash-git'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.template-ref }}

      - name: stage PKGBUILD + generate .SRCINFO (in archlinux container)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p stage
          cp deployment/aur/llamastash-git/PKGBUILD stage/PKGBUILD
          docker run --rm -v "$PWD/stage:/w" -w /w archlinux:base-devel bash -c '
            set -euo pipefail
            pacman -Sy --noconfirm --needed --quiet namcap >/dev/null
            useradd -m b
            chown -R b /w
            su -c "cd /w && makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO && namcap PKGBUILD || true" b
          '

      - name: install AUR SSH key + known_hosts
        env:
          AUR_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.AUR_SSH_KEY }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${AUR_SSH_KEY:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::AUR_SSH_KEY secret is unset; cannot push to AUR"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$AUR_SSH_KEY" >~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          ssh-keyscan -t ed25519,rsa,ecdsa aur.archlinux.org >~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: clone + push aur-llamastash-git (no-op if unchanged)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config --global user.email "release-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git config --global user.name  "llamastash-release-bot"
          git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/llamastash-git.git aur-pkg
          cp stage/PKGBUILD stage/.SRCINFO aur-pkg/
          cd aur-pkg
          git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
          if git diff-index --quiet HEAD; then
            echo "aur-llamastash-git already up to date; nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "chore(pkg): refresh llamastash-git PKGBUILD"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if git push origin master; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "push attempt ${attempt} failed; pulling --rebase and retrying"
            git pull --rebase origin master
            sleep $((attempt * 5))
          done
          echo "::error::AUR push (llamastash-git) failed after 3 attempts; inspect manually"
          exit 1

.github/workflows/publish-cargo-manual.y.text:
name: publish-cargo-manual

# Manual recovery workflow for the publish-cargo step in release.yml.
#
# Use when release.yml's publish-cargo job failed but other downstream steps
# (homebrew tap, install.sh mirror, AUR push) already succeeded — re-running
# release.yml would re-do all of those, which is wasteful and noisy. This
# workflow re-does ONLY the crates.io publish.
#
# Inputs:
#   release-tag — existing GH Release tag whose source tree is to be
#                 published (e.g. v0.0.1). The job checks out THE TAG
#                 (not main) because cargo publish's artefact is the
#                 entire source tree, not a templated file -- shipping
#                 main here would publish whatever Cargo.toml says on
#                 main, which is almost never what the operator wants.
#
# The job is idempotent: if the version is already on crates.io the publish
# is treated as success (mirrors release.yml's behaviour).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release-tag:
        description: "Existing GH Release tag to publish (e.g. v0.0.1)"
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: publish-cargo-manual-${{ inputs.release-tag }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish-cargo:
    name: publish to crates.io (manual)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: validate inputs (tag shape + release exists)
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! printf '%s' "$RELEASE_TAG" | grep -Eq '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[A-Za-z0-9.-]+)?$'; then
            echo "::error::invalid release-tag: $RELEASE_TAG (expected vX.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z-suffix)"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::no GH Release exists for tag $RELEASE_TAG in ${{ github.repository }}"
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}

      - name: cross-check Cargo.toml matches the tag
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ inputs.release-tag }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Mirrors prepare-release's check in release.yml. The published
          # crate version is whatever Cargo.toml says, NOT the tag string,
          # so a mismatch would silently ship the wrong version.
          version="${RELEASE_TAG#v}"
          cargo_version=$(awk -F\" '/^version[[:space:]]*=/ {print $2; exit}' Cargo.toml)
          # Stable + prerelease both compare exactly: the tag and Cargo.toml
          # should agree byte-for-byte at the version line.
          if [ "$cargo_version" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "::error::Cargo.toml version ($cargo_version) does not match tag ($version)."
            echo "::error::Refusing to publish — re-check out the right tag or bump Cargo.toml first."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable, 2026-05
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32  # v2

      - name: cargo publish (retry on transient crates.io errors, idempotent on already-published)
        env:
          # Pass via env, never via --token argv, so the token never appears
          # in the process table or any future `set -x` log.
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CRATES_IO_TOKEN }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::CRATES_IO_TOKEN secret is unset"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Write the stderr sidecar OUTSIDE the checkout — cargo publish's
          # dirty-tree check would otherwise reject the run with
          # "1 files in the working directory contain changes ... publish.err".
          err_log="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/cargo-publish.err"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if cargo publish --locked 2> "$err_log"; then
              echo "cargo publish succeeded on attempt ${attempt}"
              exit 0
            fi
            cat "$err_log" >&2
            # Treat "already uploaded" / "already exists" as success — happens
            # on a re-run after a workflow-level retry, or when this manual
            # workflow is invoked against an already-published tag.
            if grep -qiE 'already uploaded|already exists' "$err_log"; then
              echo "crates.io reports this version is already published; treating as success"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "cargo publish attempt ${attempt} failed; sleeping $((attempt * 15))s"
            sleep $((attempt * 15))
          done
          echo "::error::cargo publish failed 3 times; investigate crates.io status"
          exit 1

Cargo.toml.text:
[package]
name = "llamastash"
version = "0.3.0"
authors = ["Deepu K Sasidharan <d4udts@gmail.com>"]
description = "Zero-overhead, terminal-native local-LLM manager"
documentation = "https://github.com/llamastash/llamastash"
categories = ["command-line-utilities"]
keywords = ["llama-cpp", "llm", "tui", "gguf", "openai"]
repository = "https://github.com/llamastash/llamastash"
homepage = "https://github.com/llamastash/llamastash"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
edition = "2021"
rust-version = "1.95"
# `cargo run` (without --bin) targets the real binary. The fixture
# `[[bin]]` entries (fake_llama_server, fake_ds4_server) are only built
# for tests under the `test-fixtures` feature, but cargo's run-target
# picker checks the manifest before feature resolution, so we still need
# this hint.
default-run = "llamastash"
exclude = [
    # Development / packaging scaffolding — never needed by `cargo install`
    # users. The published crate must fit under crates.io's 10 MiB hard
    # limit; without these excludes the package compresses to ~16 MiB,
    # mostly from `assets/`'s marketing GIFs/screenshots.
    "test_data/*",
    "deployment/*",
    "artwork/*",
    ".github",
    ".cargo-husky/*",
    ".claude-plugin/*",
    "skills/*",
    "scripts/*",
    # Marketing media. README references are rewritten to absolute
    # https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llamastash/llamastash/main/assets/
    # URLs so the README still renders on crates.io.
    "assets/*",
    # Maintainer-internal docs subtrees. The single-file docs at
    # docs/{architecture,benchmarks,troubleshooting,usage}.md are kept
    # since they're linked from the README and useful to users browsing
    # the crate.
    "docs/brainstorms/*",
    "docs/plans/*",
    "docs/reviews/*",
    "docs/spikes/*",
    "docs/runbooks/*",
    "docs/testing/*",
    "docs/benchmarks/*",
    # Integration tests and benches are not used by binary consumers;
    # `data/benchmark-snapshot.json` is kept because it's `include_str!`'d
    # into the binary at compile time.
    "tests/*",
    "benches/*",
    # Repo-only files.
    "AGENTS.md",
    "CONTRIBUTING.md",
    "Makefile",
    "TODO.md",
    "*.log",
    "tags",
]

[dependencies]
anyhow = "1.0"
# `wayland-data-control` activates arboard's native Wayland backend
# alongside the default X11/XWayland one. Both ship together so a
# single binary works across compositors without recompilation.
arboard = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = [
    "wayland-data-control",
] }
# Bearer-token control-plane auth (Unit 1 of Windows+HTTP-IPC plan).
# `base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD` is the wire
# format for the token bytes; the dep is already in tree transitively
# via reqwest/hyper-util — declared explicitly so the daemon's auth
# module owns its surface.
base64 = { version = "0.22", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
blake3 = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
# v2 benchmark snapshot's `min_version` field gates rollback-DoS attacks
# (see Unit 1 spike). Minimal feature set keeps semver compact.
semver = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", default-features = false, features = [
    "help",
    "usage",
    "error-context",
    "derive",
    "env",
    "std",
    "color",
] }
crossterm = "0.29"
directories = "6"
# Streaming bytes for the right-pane chat tab (Unit 7) without
# pulling in tokio-stream's full surface.
futures = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
ignore = "0.4"
libc = "0.2"
log = "0.4"
notify-debouncer-mini = { version = "0.7", default-features = false }
# OS-randomness source for the per-daemon bearer token. Already in
# tree transitively via hf-hub; pulled to top-level so the auth
# module owns its dep. We only use `rand::rngs::OsRng` + `fill_bytes`
# — no PRNG state, no thread-local RNG.
rand = { version = "0.9", default-features = false, features = [
    "std",
    "os_rng",
] }
ratatui = { version = "0.30", default-features = false, features = [
    "crossterm",
    # `Paragraph::line_count` — wrap-aware row count so scroll offsets
    # clamp against rendered (wrapped) height, not logical line count.
    "unstable-rendered-line-info",
    "layout-cache",
] }
regex = { version = "1.11", default-features = false, features = [
    "std",
    "perf",
    "unicode-perl",
] }
# Pinned to 0.12 as reqwest 0.13 has issues with Send
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = [
    "json",
    "stream",
    "rustls-tls",
] }
# v2 HuggingFace pull (Unit 9). 0.5.0 is the latest stable line and
# transitively resolves the same reqwest 0.12 we pin above. Default
# features include `native-tls` + `ureq`; we want only the async
# `tokio` path on `rustls-tls`.
hf-hub = { version = "0.5", default-features = false, features = [
    "tokio",
    "rustls-tls",
] }
serde = { version = "1.0", default-features = false, features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
simplelog = { version = "0.12", default-features = false }
strum = { version = "0.28", features = ["derive"] }
# v2 init wizard (Unit 10) + 2026-05-19 interactive wizard work.
# `cliclack` replaces the unused `dialoguer` dep with a Clack-style
# stepped wizard built on `console`. Pinned by minor version so
# patches land without a deliberate PR but minor bumps don't.
cliclack = "0.5"
# Terminal styling primitives for the CLI color policy. Powers
# `cli::colors` and the prompts wrapper. Declared explicitly so the
# color/prompt modules own their dep rather than relying on the
# `cliclack`/`indicatif` transitive chain.
console = "0.16"
# Display-width measurement for terminal text (CJK paths, emoji, etc.).
# ratatui already pulls this in transitively; declaring it explicitly so
# the daemon-info pane's truncation logic can reason in cells, not chars.
unicode-width = "0.2"
sysinfo = { version = "0.39", default-features = false, features = [
    "system",
    "component",
    "disk",
] }
tokio = { version = "1.50", default-features = false, features = [
    "fs",
    "io-util",
    "macros",
    "net",
    "process",
    "rt-multi-thread",
    "signal",
    "sync",
    "time",
] }
which = "8"
# Hand-rolled error enums migrated to `thiserror` derives during the
# Tier-D audit pass (audit §3 #4).
thiserror = "2"
# `tempfile` replaces the hand-rolled atomic state-write path
# (audit §2.1 #2). Already transitive via dev-deps; pulled to
# the top level so production code can call `persist` directly.
tempfile = "3"
# tar + flate2 power the v2 install path's archive extraction
# (Unit 8). The llama.cpp GitHub Releases assets we route to on
# Linux + macOS ship as `.tar.gz`; Windows `.zip` is out of v2
# scope (post-v2 follow-up per plan Scope Boundaries).
tar = "0.4"
flate2 = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = [
    "rust_backend",
] }
sha2 = { version = "0.10", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
# Audit §2.1 #3 flagged grandchild SIGTERM leaks. The fix is a
# single character — `libc::kill(-pid, sig)` instead of
# `libc::kill(pid, sig)` — because `pre_exec` already ran
# `setsid()`, so the child's PGID equals its PID and the
# negative form signals the whole process group. Pulling in
# the `command-group` crate would boil down to the same syscall
# on Unix and is not needed.

# OpenAI-compat proxy router (post-v2 feat). Hyper 1.x is the
# lightest tokio-compatible HTTP server option and already lives in
# the dep tree transitively via reqwest. Loopback HTTP/1.1 only —
# HTTP/2 is intentionally not enabled to keep the ALPN/TLS surface
# out of the build. See docs/plans/2026-05-21-001-feat-proxy-router-plan.md
# Key Technical Decisions for the axum-vs-hyper analysis.
hyper = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = [
    "http1",
    "server",
] }
# `server-auto` would re-enable hyper's HTTP/2 feature transitively;
# we use `hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder` directly instead so
# the build stays HTTP/1.1-only. The `tokio` feature ships the
# `TokioIo` adapter that bridges hyper's `Io` traits onto
# `tokio::net::TcpStream`.
hyper-util = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["tokio"] }
http-body-util = "0.1"
# YAML stack — one family for the whole config surface. `yaml_serde` is
# the maintained serde_yaml fork (The YAML Organization, repo yaml/yaml-serde)
# and is our serde (de)serializer + `Value` type for all config reads and
# struct round-trips; it replaces the archived `serde_yaml`. `yamlpath`
# (route to a node) + `yamlpatch` (surgically patch only that node) give
# comment-/format-preserving writes — every config.yaml mutation goes through
# `config::yaml_edit` on top of these, so hand-written comments survive a
# save. All three are MIT (yamlpath/yamlpatch from zizmorcore/zizmor,
# battle-tested inside the zizmor linter) and already share `yaml_serde` as
# their value type. yamlpath/yamlpatch pinned to exact patch versions (they
# release in lockstep).
yamlpath = "=1.26.1"
yamlpatch = "=1.26.1"
yaml_serde = "=0.10.4"

# Windows-only Win32 surface for the Unit 6 process-supervision backend
# (`src/util/process_control.rs`): Job Objects for kill-on-job-close
# semantics, GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent for CTRL+BREAK delivery, and
# OpenProcess / GetExitCodeProcess for liveness probing. Pulled in only
# on `cfg(windows)` so Linux/macOS binaries don't grow.
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
windows-sys = { version = "0.61", features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_System_JobObjects",
    "Win32_System_Threading",
    "Win32_System_Console",
    # Unit 7: LockFileEx for the daemon + init-snapshot lockfile
    # backends; SetFileSecurityW + SDDL-string DACL apply for
    # state-dir secrets (`runtime.json`, `state.json`).
    "Win32_Storage_FileSystem",
    "Win32_System_IO",
    "Win32_Security",
    "Win32_Security_Authorization",
] }
# Unit 8: llama.cpp's Windows GitHub Releases assets ship as `.zip`
# (`win-cuda-*-x64.zip`, `win-vulkan-x64.zip`, etc.). Default features
# pull in bzip2 / time / aes; we only need DEFLATE so the dep stays
# small. Linux/macOS binary size is unchanged since this is
# Windows-only.
zip = { version = "5", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }
# Idiomatic Win32 COM bindings — only used for the DXGI-based GPU
# probe in `src/gpu/dxgi.rs`, which fills the Windows AMD detection
# gap (rocm-smi is Linux-only) and also covers Intel + the rare
# NVIDIA-without-nvidia-smi.exe stripped-install case. Sibling of
# `windows-sys` 0.61; only the requested features compile.
windows = { version = "0.61", features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_Graphics_Dxgi",
    "Win32_Graphics_Dxgi_Common",
    # D3D12's architecture feature query exposes the authoritative `UMA`
    # flag — the only reliable way on Windows to tell a genuine
    # unified-memory APU (Strix Halo / Phoenix / iGPU) from a discrete
    # card. `SharedSystemMemory` in the DXGI desc is ~half system RAM on
    # *every* adapter, so it can't carry that signal.
    "Win32_Graphics_Direct3D",
    "Win32_Graphics_Direct3D12",
] }

[lib]
name = "llamastash"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "llamastash"
path = "src/main.rs"
bench = false

# Test-only fake `llama-server` exposed under a feature flag so it
# never ships in `cargo install`-built artefacts. Integration tests
# spawn this via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake_llama_server`.
[[bin]]
name = "fake_llama_server"
path = "tests/fixtures/fake_llama_server.rs"
required-features = ["test-fixtures"]
bench = false
test = false
doc = false

# Test-only fake `lemond` umbrella (OpenAI-compatible) under the same
# feature flag. Integration tests spawn it via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake_lemond`.
[[bin]]
name = "fake_lemond"
path = "tests/fixtures/fake_lemond.rs"
required-features = ["test-fixtures"]
bench = false
test = false
doc = false

# Fake `ds4-server` for the ds4 backend integration tests — mirrors the real
# load-before-listen + fixed-alias + no-/health contract. Spawned via
# `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake_ds4_server`; injected as `ds4.binary` per-test.
[[bin]]
name = "fake_ds4_server"
path = "tests/fixtures/fake_ds4_server.rs"
required-features = ["test-fixtures"]
bench = false
test = false
doc = false

# Fake `vllm` launcher for the vLLM backend integration tests — mirrors the
# slow engine-init window and the served-model-name contract readiness keys
# on. Spawned via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake_vllm_server`; injected as
# `backend.vllm.servers[0].binary` per-test.
[[bin]]
name = "fake_vllm_server"
path = "tests/fixtures/fake_vllm_server.rs"
required-features = ["test-fixtures"]
bench = false
test = false
doc = false

# Local-only git hooks installed at first `cargo test` (or any
# build that resolves dev-dependencies). The hook bodies live in
# `.cargo-husky/hooks/`; pre-commit reformats + lints and pre-push
# additionally runs the full test suite so wedged commits never
# leave the laptop. `user-hooks` makes cargo-husky install our
# scripts verbatim instead of its built-in defaults.
[dev-dependencies.cargo-husky]
version = "1"
default-features = false
features = ["user-hooks"]

# Criterion drives the proxy-overhead bench landed by Unit 7 of the
# proxy-router plan. Default features pull in `rayon` + `plotters`
# (the SVG plot backend) which would more than double the dev-dep
# tree; `html_reports` is sufficient to produce the maintainer-
# readable summary the runbook expects. The bench itself is feature-
# gated under `test-fixtures` so plain `cargo build --benches`
# without that feature is a no-op for downstream packagers.
[dev-dependencies.criterion]
version = "0.5"
default-features = false
features = ["html_reports"]

# Bench harness for R160 latency validation. `harness = false` is
# criterion's idiom: we hand-roll `main` in the bench file so
# criterion's macros own the driver rather than libtest. See
# `docs/runbooks/proxy-latency-bench.md` for the reproducible run
# procedure.
[[bench]]
name = "proxy_overhead"
harness = false
required-features = ["test-fixtures"]

[features]
